title: Tests-first git evidence: 10 modules have RED commits with combined scopes the gate cannot parse; gaps/align/uv/mcp/viewer/frontend have none at all; app committed tests after implementation. Not fabricating retroactive commits.
Ten module CLAUDE.md/README.md files still say RED by design / raises NotImplementedError for modules that are fully green.

Primary-button hover fails WCAG AA at 2.87:1. DESIGN.md typography scale never reached tokens.css so app.css hardcodes off-scale px. No main landmark, no h1. Action log rebuilds the whole DOM inside an aria-live region on every append.
Object creation degrades 17x from 3.16ms to 54.52ms per op between 100 and 900 objects (a view_layer.update() per object). The stated target is thousands.
snapshot() walks mesh.polygons, so a vertex referenced by no face is invisible on real Blender. measure.find_loose_or_duplicate is dead code against real geometry while working against the fake.

Nothing in the production wiring computes a snapshot_path, so raw execution either raises or records an unrestorable barrier. Undo across it re-runs the arbitrary script instead of restoring - SECURITY.md claims this defence and it does not exist.
A dead writer wedges the lock forever: lease expiry is measured against document.head, but head only advances through apply, which only the dead lease holder can call.

A handler that creates objects then raises leaves them live in the engine with no log entry - add_railing failing on its 3rd create_mesh left 29 orphans. They show in the live view as geometry with no history and vanish on the next save/load.

distance and gap_width are computed from world AABBs only. Two beams yawed 45 degrees and 1.4m apart report distance 0.0 while find_clipping reports a 0.1m interpenetration between parts that never touch. Every test uses an unrotated cube.

find_clipping reports min per-axis AABB overlap as magnitude and feeds it to JoineryIntent.permits. For anything thinner than it is deep - every post, dowel, tenon - the number collapses to the cross-section. A post 500mm through a deck reports 0.1m, and a declared 150mm socket silences it entirely.
npm run test:backend called python, the Windows Store stub. The documented command never worked and the gate read the suite as red. Now resolves a working interpreter.
Three duplicated copies of the degenerate-triangle guard used 1e-12 where normalized() raises below EPSILON. detail hit this and was fixed; the copies never were.
MESH_UPSERT carries a transform the browser never applied; every object rendered at the world origin and a positioned object snapped back there on its next topology change.

export scaled each mesh in place but left its translation in metres; two-object scenes landed 3.57x wrong for Roblox and 100x for Unreal. mirror_x flipped meshes without moving them. Verified by a test that reads node translations out of the written GLB.
promote() logged a phase_promotion operation no handler could execute, so the phase machine could not advance at all.
perform() emitted hardcoded 0.0 placeholder measurements; B-000 was marked closed but the wiring was never done. Now calls measure against scene.engine and populates new_problems.

perform() never forwarded the write lease to scene.apply(); every mutating call through the real agent path raised LockContention against its own just-verified lease. Reported independently by 5 finders.

ScenePort exposes no EngineProtocol, so Orchestrator.perform cannot run real measurements — the check-after-every-geometry-change loop currently carries placeholder Measurements. This is the products core promise (Gate A 3.1 + ADR-005) and must be wired before Phase 5.

engine.snapshot() assumed every mesh was already triangulated (a comment said so outright). True for geometry it created, false for Blenders own startup cube and every imported asset or hand-modelled .blend — so snapshot() raised on the first outside mesh and measure could not inspect exactly the geometry a user most wants checked. Now fan-triangulates; polygon_count preserves the face count.

bevel_edges resolved edge_indices as (vertex,vertex) pairs, matching two conformance checks that had drifted from the contracts Sequence[int]. detail follows the contract and passed ints, so the real consumer raised TypeError on first use while both suites stayed green. The engine agent flagged this honestly in testsSuspect. Contract form is now primary.

_triangle_normal called normalized() unconditionally and raised on degenerate slivers, which real Blender bevels produce. realism_report crashed on exactly the post-bevel geometry it exists to assess. Never caught because FakeEngines bevel duplicates a face rather than producing real geometry.

Defect.describe() emitted a set-intersection sign and reports used bullet characters; cp1252 is the default Windows console encoding and cannot encode them, so printing a clipping defect raised UnicodeEncodeError on the primary target platform. ASCII in machine-readable report text, UTF-8 forced at the CLI entry point, regression test encodes every report string as cp1252.
build_app did not reset the engine, so Blenders startup cube/camera/light were in every session and showed up in object counts, clipping checks and exports as geometry the agent never made.

add_railing sockets posts and balusters into whatever it is mounted on but declares no JoineryIntent, so a stair-plus-railing reports 94 clipping defects an agent must dismiss one by one. The railing should declare its own joinery for the parts it deliberately embeds.

Real Blender bevel produces a mean triangle aspect ratio of ~116 and edge-length CoV ~1.6 on a simple tread — very poor topology. The tool measures and reports this correctly; the bevel itself needs better parameters or a cleanup pass.

ScenePort declared document() as a method; Scene exposes it as a property. Both consumers matched the declaration and wrote doubles that matched it too, so three suites passed while the real trio could never work together. Found only by the end-to-end suite.

ops.validate_params expected Vec3; an agent sends JSON lists. ops documented conversion as belonging at the boundary and nobody built the boundary, so every point-taking operation raised AttributeError on first real agent contact. Coerced at the composition root, schema-driven so add_lod_chain ratios are not mistaken for a coordinate.

Four transport tests asserted the MCP SDK was absent - an assertion about the machine, not the code. They inverted the moment the declared dependency was installed. Now simulate absence; a new test fails loudly if the package rename is undone.
src/mcp shadowed the mcp PyPI SDK so `import mcp` in our own transports resolved to us — the SDK was permanently unreachable and no subscription client could ever connect. Renamed to src/mcp_server.

ops+gaps+align all correctly declared ToolRole.REFINE, totalling 19 tools in one role against an 8-tool bound. The registrys fair-cap fallback then silently hid repair, make_plumb and close_visual_gap. Split REPAIR and ALIGN into their own roles; every role now sits inside 1-8 with nothing hidden.
